einzeiler: Former Navy SEAL Andy Stumpf on risk, podcasts, and living life after combat.
kurzfassung: Former Navy SEAL and podcast host Andy Stumpf joins the show to discuss his military career, combat injuries, and the realities of special operations. He reflects on his transition to civilian life, extreme skydiving and base jumping, and how he manages risk and mental focus. The conversation also explores the evolving landscape of podcasting, modern media, and the importance of engaged communities.
stichpunkte: Andy Stumpf reflects on his 18-year career as a Navy SEAL, multiple combat deployments, and earning five Bronze Stars.
He discusses being shot at close range by an AK-47 during combat, resulting in severe nerve damage and a long recovery.
The conversation covers his transition to professional skydiving and wingsuit base jumping, and why he eventually stopped.
Stumpf explains how high-risk environments and extreme sports help individuals achieve a mental flow state and block out everyday distractions.
He shares his perspective on the current podcasting industry, audience engagement, and why he avoids the pursuit of massive scale.
The discussion touches on the flaws and subjective nature of military awards systems and modern civilian recognition.
Stumpf talks about his move to Montana and his involvement with organizations like the Navy SEAL Foundation.
He offers insights on handling risk logically, avoiding the trap of chasing money, and finding purpose after leaving the military.

kapitel.titel: Military Service and the Reality of Combat
Military Awards and the Awards System
Reflections on Risk and Extreme Sports
Life in Montana and Final Thoughts

clips.hook: Would you give back your Bronze Star for a cocktail napkin?
clips.text: The guest compares modern military commendations to World War II citations, joking that his own awards pale in comparison to legendary acts of heroism.

clips.hook: How a bullet missed a fatal path by inches
clips.text: A harrowing close-up account of taking enemy fire, getting pinned under a vehicle, and a second round burning along a belt.

clips.hook: Spitting into the wind before a 486-foot bridge jump
clips.text: The guest describes the intense physical and mental preparation required for base jumping, including using a simple spit test to check wind conditions.

clips.hook: Why the most resoundingly boring person hosts a podcast
clips.text: The guest explains that his show succeeds because he is genuinely fascinated by other people rather than trying to talk about himself.

clips.hook: The mental headspace that replaces combat adrenaline
clips.text: An explanation of how extreme activities force complete mental focus and provide a temporary escape from daily pressures.

beschreibung:
Andy Stumpf knows what it takes to operate when everything goes wrong. A former Navy SEAL who served with SEAL Team Six, Stumpf spent 17 years in the military, including a tour as a BUD/S instructor responsible for training hundreds of aspiring SEALs. He was also shot at close range by an Iraqi insurgent with an AK-47—and somehow came back to serve again.
In this episode, Andy pulls back the curtain on the world of special operations and the psychology of becoming a SEAL. He reveals what he learned about the candidates who ring the bell, the methods he used as an instructor to get them to keep going—or make them quit—and what it really feels like when an AK-47 fragment shatters your sciatic nerve. It's a conversation about fear, pain, endurance, and the strange things that happen in your head when the stakes couldn't be higher.
Andy is the host of Cleared Hot, one of the most popular podcasts devoted to military life, special operations, and the people who have lived it.
